data.one_liner: Flutter widget to inspect and edit key‑value storage such as shared_preferences.
data.what_it_does: Provides a UI (StorageView) that connects to a StorageDriver to read, update, and delete values from any key‑value storage backend. Developers can plug in existing drivers or implement their own to view data at runtime.
use_when: You need a quick UI to debug or verify stored preferences during development
You want to support multiple storage backends (shared_preferences, flutter_secure_storage) with a single inspector
avoid_when: Running in production where exposing storage UI is a security risk
You only need programmatic access without a UI
strengths: Works with any storage via a driver interface
Responsive UI works on mobile, desktop and web
Low integration effort – just add dependency and provide a driver
weaknesses: Limited to key‑value style storage, no SQL table browsing
Package is still in early development (dev version)
No built‑in support for secure storage encryption UI

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: Direct programmatic access to preferences without UI overhead

alternatives.name: flutter_secure_storage
alternatives.why_pick_it: Secure storage access when UI inspection is not required

data.minimal_example:
final driver = MockStorageDriver();
Scaffold(body: StorageView(storageDriver: driver));
